programRef: PLAYER SHIP program, increment 1 of 4 (see intent.md 'Program')
designDecisions: One GLB holds exterior hull AND cockpit interior (Max). Eye-point convention carried over from cockpit.glb: 1 unit = 1 m, Y-up, no scale normalisation, forward = -Z.

Length 16-20 m: SHIP_HULL_LENGTHS_M.player = 20 (src/core/ScaleConstants.js:154), Max allows 'slightly smaller'. Bubble outer width 1.8-3.0 m: helicopter-cabin scale per Max; the shipped cockpit.glb is 2.56 m wide, inside the range.
Triangle ceiling 3,000: derived as shipped cockpit.glb (782) + canon freighter-class hull budget (1,500), rounded up for the bubble glass and struts. A prototype ceiling, not a target.
Display plan comes BEFORE concept art: the number and placement of displays decide the mounts and consoles in the model.
Astra jobs follow the astra skill loop (2d sheet -> CC sheet review -> 3d -> CC model review). Every Astra output is a PLACEHOLDER (memory: well-dipper-ai-assets-are-placeholders).
Lab page is a new root-level HTML (player-ship-lab.html), sibling of cockpit-lab.html; no src/ edits.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A display plan, worked out with Max, says how many displays the cockpit has, where each sits, and what each shows (the system you're in; the selected star/planet/moon/object; speed and status), and every item it lists is a value the sim actually tracks today, each with a src/ file:line.

verifyVia.observable: Each listed readout cites a src/ file:line that produces it; no fuel/hull/heat/cargo/shield readout appears; Max's sign-off sentence is quoted verbatim.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Astra concept sheets exist for the exterior (Chris Foss references) and the helicopter-bubble cockpit, each passed the CC sheet review, staged at a Windows path, and Max's chosen direction is recorded verbatim.

verifyVia.input: Open each job's sheet-review.md and UAT.md under .astra/jobs/
verifyVia.observable: sheet-review.md rows all PASS; the sheet PNG exists at the staged C:\Users\Max\Documents\Blender\astra\well-dipper-trunk\... path; UAT.md holds Max's pick in his words.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: One GLB contains both the ship's exterior and its bubble cockpit interior, at 16-20 m long, with a 1.8-3.0 m wide bubble, at most 3,000 triangles, flat matte materials, no cameras or lights, and an Eye_Point node inside the bubble.

verifyVia.observable: bbox long axis 16-20 m; tris <= 3000; cameras 0; lights 0; textures 0; node Eye_Point present, and its position lies inside the bubble's bounds.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: INTERFACE.md next to the model lists everything the game may depend on (scale, origin, axes, every required node name and material slot), and the GLB conforms to it, so a hand-made replacement that meets the list drops in with no code change.

verifyVia.input: Run the conformance check named in INTERFACE.md against player-ship.glb, then against a GLB with Eye_Point renamed
verifyVia.observable: Real GLB: PASS. Sabotaged GLB: FAIL naming Eye_Point (liveness probe).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: HOW-TO-REBUILD.md next to the model gives Max, as a beginner Blender user, a head start on hand-modelling it: purpose, key measurements, the reference images, a step order, which parts are free to redesign versus fixed by INTERFACE.md, and how to export and drop it in.

verifyVia.observable: All six sections present; every measurement matches the probe's numbers for the shipped GLB; export steps name the exporter settings that INTERFACE.md requires.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: docs/AI-PLACEHOLDERS.md lists every AI-made file in the repo that could reach a build, marked placeholder or replaced, including this increment's GLB and sheets, and flags the grey-area files (Claude-scripted cockpit.glb and fighter GLBs, AI concept sheets used only as reference).

verifyVia.observable: Every GLB under public/assets/ appears in the register with an origin and status; the new player-ship.glb is marked placeholder.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: In player-ship-lab.html, one key press flies the camera from the outside view (behind and a little above the ship, mouse-orbitable) into the pilot's seat at the game's FOV, and the same key flies it back out, as a quick animation rather than a cut.

verifyVia.input: Open player-ship-lab.html in chrome-devtools, press the toggle key from outside, sample camera position each frame; press again from inside
verifyVia.observable: Camera position changes over >= 0.25 s and <= 1.0 s with at least 10 intermediate frames (not a cut); ends within 1 cm of Eye_Point at the game FOV inside, and at the outside pose behind/above the ship; no console errors.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Nothing the game loads changes: no file under src/ is modified and the existing cockpit.glb is untouched.

Max flies in and out in the lab and judges: the cockpit feels appropriately sized compared to the ship, the view works inside and outside, and the ship reads as 'woah cool, I've never seen that kind of ship in a game before'.

verifyVia.input: Max opens player-ship-lab.html, orbits the ship, presses the toggle key in and out several times
